systems.part: lower town, western and southern fortification

main_system_reason: The eastern fortification is the longest Harappan line on the plan with exposed stretches along its length, and the 1983-84 plan gives the same direction for it within about one degree. The other sides of the circuit are drawn largely as conjecture and are not square to it, and the streets run obliquely, so Banawali has no single orthogonal layout to report.
notes: We measured the two site plans that Bisht published in Indian Archaeology - A Review for 1983-84 (Fig. 4) and 1987-88 (Fig. 1). Both arrows are lettered only N. Banawali is not laid out on an orthogonal grid: the fortified circuit is a trapezium whose northern side is turned clockwise and whose eastern side is turned anticlockwise from the plan's north by about ten degrees each, the western and southern sides run within about five degrees of the plan's north and east, the wall between acropolis and lower town is curved, and the streets run obliquely. We report each side of the circuit as its own system and treat the eastern fortification, which has exposed stretches along its length, as the best-controlled line. Most of the northern, western and southern lines are drawn as conjecture or as pre-Harappan defences in the legends, so their confidence is low. Both figures are low-resolution scans (738 x 908 and 794 x 1008 px), but the lines are long. No final report on Banawali is available to us.
